Coloscopie est le podcast d'entretiens l: Coloscopie ("Colonoscopy") is the interview podcast launched by Laurent Baffie two years ago. The concept: he hosts artists and personalities he likes to "give them a colonoscopy" — to go deep, beyond their latest releases or projects. He pushes them out of their comfort zone with his usual style, but kindly.
On connaît surtout Baffie comme le snipe: Baffie is best known as Ardisson's sniper for more than 30 years, from Double Jeu to Salut les Terriens. But this is different: it's his show of maturity. Polished production, a cosy dimmed atmosphere, Shure mics, audio and video release, and a theme tune by Bob Sinclar. Joined by Romane, he gives speech time to breathe: episodes from 40 minutes to 1h30.
Baffie use de son image d'humoriste prov: Baffie plays on his image as a provocative comedian without overdoing it, and offers a space where guests reveal themselves differently. Caustic humour mixes with very genuine moments — "tease the ones you love".
Le format long révèle qu'au-delà du trub: The long format reveals that beyond the troublemaker, there's a sincere love of talent. We also discover Baffie as a defender of animals and nature, his friendships, his passions — in an authentic light.
40 ans de carrière et un réseau immense: 40 years of career and a huge network guarantee a steady flow of quality guests: Gad Elmaleh, Les Inconnus, Philippe Geluck, Béatrice Dalle, Manu Payet, Josiane Balasko & Marilou Berry… Solid Apple Podcasts rating: 4.5/5.
L'intérêt principal, c'est le contraste: The main appeal is the contrast: a provocateur's image AND a space where guests open up sincerely. Unlike timed or promo-driven formats, Baffie gives the conversation time — even if it means losing those who only want action or easy laughs.
Verdict : Baffie est un grand interviewe: Verdict: Baffie is a great interviewer. His "tease the ones you love" style can be disconcerting if taken literally, but you have a good time, with real moments of emotion. If you like long, sincere interviews with a touch of irony, this podcast is worth a listen. If you prefer pure stand-up or short formats, it may be a bit too introspective.
